newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan firms bid to purchase marketing board.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan firms bid to purchase marketing board.

text.p: A consortium of five Ugandan companies is pressing the government to reopen bidding for the Coffee Marketing Board Ltd (CMBL) six months after Swiss company Sucafina emerged as the sole bidder.

Under the umbrella Uganda Consortium of Agro-Processors (AGACAP), the companies have placed a new bid of $5.5 million. But bids have already officially closed and it was not known whether government departments would consider it.

AGACAP Chairman Jamada Lutta Musoke told reporters on Tuesday that it was "unwise to sell a strategic concern such as the board to foreign buyers" and said Sucafina would be welcomed into the consortium if the company made a formal request.

In December, the Ugandan government said it rejected a $3.3 million Sucafina bid for 51 percent of the CMBL and Minister of state (deputy minister) for privatisation Matthew Rukikaire said Sucafina would succeed only by raising its bid.
But since then the privatisation unit has been in further talks with Sucafina and a final decision on whether the Swiss firm gets CMBL was expected by end-April, Rukikaire's office said.

Rukikaire told the daily Monitor newspaper on Tuesday that Sucafina was the only company to show interest when the government called for bids for the board two years ago and it would be unfair to call for fresh bids.
"If UGACAP had come earlier, we would have gone to the Divestiture Reform Implementation Committee and convinced them to negotiate with the Consortium," Rukikaire said.

"Sucafina are the only people who submitted a bid when we advertised. It would be improper if we short-changed the process to favour new interested parties in complete disregard to the initial sole bidder. The process would become a disaster."
Musoke said UGACAP's main worry was that giving the board's processing and storage unit to one buyer, which could also be a competitor, would be unfair in the coffee export business.

CMBL assets included in the earlier offer were valued at $36.7 million. The company's principal asset is its processing and storage unit in Bugoolobi. It has an export processing capacity of four million 60-kg bags a year.

Previously, Ugandan privatisation officials have said that a bidder which offered two-thirds of the value price would be considered serious, but if one was not found then they would be comfortable selling at a lower price only to Ugandan investors.

Geneva-based Sucafina was the only bidder for the CMBL stake, submitting its bid two minutes before the deadline on September 26. It had offered to buy the 51 percent stake in two tranches, one of $1.8 million and a second of $1.5 million.
CMBL's market share in the coffee export business fell to 9.4 percent in 1995, compared to around 84 percent four years earlier. Uganda has more than 100 private coffee exporters.
Uganda is Africa's leading coffee producer and plans to export around four million bags in 1996/97 compared to around 4.2 million bags in 1995/96. Coffee is its predominant foreign exchange earner.
